title: Daily Briefing — Friday, October 2
coverage: Covering roughly Thursday morning through Friday midday MDT. NYT technology/science/business sections were again blocked to automated fetching this run, so NYT-originated reporting below is cited via outlets that reference it.

top.headline: Orbital data centers went from paper to hardware in a single day
top.summary: Google published peer-reviewed analysis in Joule concluding that space-based compute needs roughly 1,800 Starship flights over a decade and about $200/kg launch costs to pencil out. Hours later its first Project Suncatcher test satellite actually launched on Transporter-18 with Tensor Processing Units aboard.

top.headline: The Pentagon is standing up a four-star command for autonomous warfare
top.summary: AUTOWARCOM will consolidate drone and autonomy efforts from across the services, DIU, and JIATF-401 into one global joint command with its own budget and acquisition authority. It is targeted to be established 1 October 2027.

top.headline: SpaceX had its busiest day of the year
top.summary: Crew-13 reached the ISS in 7 hours 50 minutes, the fastest Crew Dragon ascent ever, and Falcon Heavy flew its first-ever National Reconnaissance Office mission that night. It capped a day in which SpaceX recovered four boosters.

items.headline: OpenAI dismissed three safety researchers over alleged information handling
items.summary: Per WSJ reporting, an internal probe found they shared confidential material with an outside AI-safety organization. It lands two days after NYT reporting that executives had brushed off internal safety warnings, and shortly after OpenAI shelved the GPT-6.1 "Astra" launch.

items.headline: "Decision models" are becoming a real product category
items.summary: AWS open-sourced Strands Decider 2B, a Qwen3.5-2B derivative that outputs calibrated choices among predefined options with confidence scores instead of text, small enough to run locally. OpenAI shipped something similar the same week. The engineering appeal is concrete: a workflow step with bounded outputs, lower latency, and a confidence number you can threshold on, which is a far better fit for autonomy stacks than free-form generation.

items.headline: Reporting says Grok influenced the Venezuela decision
items.summary: Time, with context from the Atlantic and NYT, reports Trump questioned Grok for hours in a December 2025 meeting with Musk about likely Venezuelan reaction, and credited the chatbot afterward. The piece notes Grok was also in use during June 2026 Iran strikes while Musk co-leads a Pentagon battlefield-technology study, an unusually direct conflict-of-interest question for AI in national-security decision loops.

items.headline: Agent-first consumer products keep shipping
items.summary: Shopify launched Canvas, which builds storefronts through conversation, and ChatGPT added virtual clothing try-on. Individually minor, together they mark the shift from chat as an answer box to chat as the application shell.

items.headline: Crew-13 launched and set a Dragon speed record
items.summary: Falcon 9 (booster B1101, third flight) lifted Dragon "Grace" from Cape Canaveral at 11:10 a.m. EDT Oct 1 with Jessica Watkins, Luke Delaney, Joshua Kutryk (CSA), and Sergey Teteryatnikov (Roscosmos). Docking came 7h50m after liftoff, the fastest Crew Dragon rendezvous to date, which means a tighter phasing window and fewer catch-up burns. The mission had slipped two weeks on an oxidizer leak found in August.

items.headline: Falcon Heavy flew its first NRO mission
items.summary: NROL-97 lifted from LC-39A at 11:53 p.m. EDT on a northeasterly, high-energy trajectory; side boosters B1104 and B1072 (both fresh off the Roman Space Telescope launch) returned to LZ-1 and LZ-2 while core B1106 was expended. It was the NRO's first Falcon Heavy after 22 Falcon 9 missions, and SpaceX's third launch of the day.

items.headline: Transporter-18 put 130 payloads into SSO
items.summary: Launched from Vandenberg SLC-4E on booster B1082's 26th flight (RTLS landing), the 110th Falcon 9 of 2026. Aboard: Starfish Space's 335 kg Otter for the SSPICY mission, which will autonomously close to within hundreds of meters of dead satellites to characterize spin rates and surface condition; Google's Suncatcher M1; the SPRITE 12U supernova-shock CubeSat; and Varda W-8 and W-9 orbital factories with return capsules.

items.headline: Google put real numbers on space-based compute
items.summary: The Joule paper models an 81-satellite close-formation constellation for parallel processing, needing roughly 180 Starship flights per year at 200 t each for a decade, and $200/kg by 2035 (extrapolating SpaceX's roughly 20%/yr cost decline). Radiation-induced chip error rates look tolerable for inference but not for months-long training runs, the honest limiting constraint.

items.headline: Canada is getting its first large-scale rocket engine test site
items.summary: Canada Rocket Company will build the facility in London, Ontario. It is notable because engine test infrastructure, not design, is usually the long-pole item for a new national launch capability.

items.headline: AUTOWARCOM: a four-star command for drones, AI and robotics
items.summary: Announced Sept 30 by Secretary Hegseth, with Owen West (DIU) guiding implementation and a commander to be named. It folds in the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group and JIATF-401 under a new Direct Reporting Program Manager for Unmanned Systems, and unlike SOUTHCOM's regional autonomous warfare command (April 2026) it is global and joint. For anyone on a UAV program, this is the clearest signal yet that autonomy procurement is getting its own service-like budget line.

items.headline: TSMC is weighing another multibillion-dollar Texas campus, and warning its biggest customers
items.summary: Bloomberg reports the new site study; separately TSMC told Nvidia and Broadcom to expect an advanced-packaging capacity squeeze as AI demand outruns CoWoS buildout. Packaging, not wafers, remains the bottleneck.

items.headline: California set hard operational rules for robotaxis
items.summary: Newsom signed SB 1246: penalties if an AV blocks first responders more than 30 minutes, remote operators must be US-based and US-licensed, local incident technicians must be dispatchable, and jurisdictions must be told vehicle locations during system-wide failures. Effective July 2028, hitting Waymo, Tesla and Zoox. These are the first rules that treat degraded-mode response as a design requirement, not a policy.

items.headline: Fervo brought the first enhanced geothermal plant online in 23 months
items.summary: Cape Station's first phase delivers 33 MW of a planned 100 MW (long-term ambition: 4 GW), built with horizontal drilling and fracturing techniques borrowed straight from shale oil and gas. Google and Southern California Edison are among the offtakers. Firm, 24/7 power is the scarce input for AI datacenters.

items.headline: Drone inspection keeps winning long-term utility contracts
items.summary: Cyberhawk signed a three-year extension with SSE to inspect UK electricity networks, and DroneLife reports defense-hardened airframes and sensors migrating into commercial BVLOS work. Grid inspection is becoming the volume commercial BVLOS use case, which is what pulls Part 108-class rulemaking forward.

items.headline: Tesla's Roadster reveal slipped two weeks to Oct 15, because of wind
items.summary: Musk postponed the Waco, Texas event over high winds and flood alerts, noting it can only be held outdoors. The reason it must be outdoors is the SpaceX cold-gas thruster package Tesla claims will cut 0-60 mph to roughly one second; reservations remain $50,000, Founders Series $250,000. A demo that needs open air and calm weather tells you how much of the performance claim rides on reaction-control thrust rather than tires.

items.headline: VW-backed Gotion claims a sulfide solid-state cell at 400 Wh/kg and a $150/kWh target
items.summary: Up from the 350 Wh/kg previously claimed for its Jinshi cells, with puncture and high-temperature tests reportedly producing neither smoke nor flame. A 2 GWh pilot line was locked in March 2026; no mass-production date yet. CATL and BYD are both aiming at 2027, so take the cost figure as a target, not a price.

items.headline: Hamilton warned and Ferrari fined 10,000 euros at the Bahrain GP, which is being held at Sepang
items.summary: Stewards found Hamilton unnecessarily impeded Bortoleto's Audi in FP2 by moving onto the racing line at low speed; the aggravating factor was Ferrari failing to call traffic over the radio despite knowing his right-hand mirror was damaged. The race carries Bahrain's name in Malaysia because the original April round was cancelled amid the Iran conflict and Bahrain is funding the relocated event.

items.headline: Sepang's 2017-vintage asphalt is the real story of the weekend
items.summary: Drivers report very low grip, "incredibly aggressive" surface character and loose stones picked up inside track limits after three months of inactivity. Leclerc called it very slippery; Bearman likened it to Bahrain. Expect mixed two- and three-stop strategies as degradation, not fuel or energy deployment, sets the race.

items.headline: One year after the US EV tax credit ended, the market has found a floor, and hybrids took the upside
items.summary: EV share peaked at 11.4% in Sept 2025, fell 36% in late 2025 and 27% year over year in Q1 2026, and has settled at 5-6% through 2026. Hybrid sales rose 27% annually, with Kia's up 99% year over year in August. Over 300,000 EVs come off lease within a year, which is the next real test of residuals.

engineersCorner.headline: Thermal, not compute or launch, is the real constraint on orbital data centers
engineersCorner.body: 1,800 Starship flights at 200 t each is about 360,000 tonnes to orbit, roughly 500x everything humanity has launched to date, and that is Google's own stated price of admission. The honest constraint in the same work is smaller and more interesting: the Suncatcher prototype can only run its TPU in 15-minute bursts because the satellite's power and thermal management can't sustain the load. In space there is no convection, so every watt has to leave by radiation, and by Stefan-Boltzmann the heat rejected per unit area goes as T^4, so the required radiator area for a fixed load falls steeply with radiator temperature. Thermal, not compute or launch cost, is the thing that decides whether this works.

footnote: Compiled from public reporting across the outlets linked above. Emailed edition sent the same morning.
